Mr. Moudud Ahmed with Ms. Ireen Mahbub ------ for the accused-petitioner

Mr. M. Farooque, Deputy Attorney General with Mr. Syed Abu Kowser, Assistant Attorney General, Mr. Golam Ashique, Assistant Attorney General, Mr. Mushfiqur Rahman, Assistant Attorney General and Mr. Md. Mamunor Rashid, Assistant Attorney General ------ for the State.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, J: The accused-petitioner Captain (Rtd.) Nurul Huda having been depicted as one of the killers of Abdur Rab Serniabat, former Minister Irrigation. Flood Control and Water Resources of the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh some members of his family and inmates of his house and also as one of perpetrators of causing grievous bullet injuries on some members of his family and inmates of the house in the incident that took place in catty morning on August 15, 1975 stands indicted along with other accused persons for offence punishable under Sections 12013/149/448/326/307/302/201/297 and 34 of the Penal Code in Ramna Police Station Case No. 93 dated 21.10.1996 registered on the strength of First Information Report laid by Mrs. Sahan Ara Begum, daughter-in-law of Abdur Rab Serniabat as Informant. 

 2. The case projected in First Information. Report is that at about 4-30 to 5-00 A.M. on August 15, 1975 Informant and other inmates of the house situated at 27 Mintoo Road. Dhaka woke up from bed on hearing sounds of gun fire. Informant and other members of family went to the room of her father-in-law. Abdur Rab Serniabat and closed door. The accused-petitioner accused Major Shahriar, Major Aziz Pasha and Captain Mazed being armed with automatic fire arms went to upstairs of the building and forcibly broke open the door, compelled Informant, Abdur Rab Serniabat and others to get down to down stair. The accused petitioner, accused Major Shahriar and accused Captain Mazed will fire arms in their hands fired at them indiscriminately and her father-in-law Abdur Rab Serniabat, her son. Babu Serniabat aged four years, brother-in-law Advocate Abdus Shahid Serniabat, sister-in-law Baby Serniabat, brother-in-law Arif Serniabat and others died on the spot. The Informant, her mother-in-law Ameena Begum, sister-in-law Rina Serniabat and others sustained bullet injuries. Her husband Abul Hasnat Abdullah miraculously could save himself. Informant could recognize accused-petitioner, Major Shahriar, accused Major Pasha and accused Captain Majed as assailants. Delay in laying First Information Report was explained in the way that law could not be set in motion on account of political pressure and security and on establishment of rule of law and political stability First Information Report was lodged. 

 4. Application for bail was presented before Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 7.11.1996 and 5.4.1997 but without any success. Bail was then sought before learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1652 of 1997. Learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka by order dated 6.5.1997 refused to enlarge accused-petitioner on bail. 

 5. The accused-petitioner thereafter approached this Court in invoking jurisdiction under Section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short The Code) for grant of bail and obtained Rule. The petition has been numbered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1965 of 1997. 

 6. Statements made in petition for bail have been also grounds in support of bail which arc that the accused-petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case and no charge sheet has been submitted though six months had already elapsed and the provision of Section 167(5) of The Code had not been complied with and it is not sure when Police Report will be submitted and trial will commence. The accused petitioner has been suffering from serious heart diseases and his health condition is detorioting day by day and the prosecution case is based on hearsay evidence. 

 7. Good number of Supplementary Affidavits of different dates have been filed for and on behalf of accused petitioner with statements that he is innocent and is in no way connected with commission of crime and that he has been suffering from various ailments and for humanitarian around lie may be released on bail and that Prof. Atai Rabbi of PG Hospital opined for his surgery and that there is no chance of commencement of trial in view of recording an order of stay staying proceedings of the case by a Division Bench of High Court Division in Criminal Revision No. 123 of 2000 laid by co-accused Taheruddin Thakur. 

 8. Statements made in petition for hail and also Supplementary Affidavits have been controverted from the side of State by way of Affidavit-in-Opposition, Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition and Affidavit-in-Reply raising contentions that the accused petitioner is directly involved in the killing of Abdur Rab Serniabat and his other family members-and witnesses examined under Section 161 of The Code implicated accused petitioner in commission of crime and accused petitioner got connection with powerful civilians and politicians outside country and if enlarged on bail he will not be available for trial and that the alleged advice allegedly  given by Prof. Atai Rabbi does not appear to have been initiatted by Prof. Atai Rabbi and Doctors of P.G. Hospital forming a Board dated 17.5.1998 recorded opinion that further stay in the Hospital was not necessary and that accused petitioner had been given status of a Division-1 prisoner in jail by order of High Court Division arid the case already stood transferred to court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge for trial and out of seventeen (17) accused persons eleven (11) had absconded and in the event of granting bail to accused-petitioner he may abscond and it will be difficult for prosecution to bring witnesses in court. 

 i.	The accused petitioner played no part in the killing of Abdur Rab Serniabat, his family members and inmates of the house and he has been falsely implicated in the case out of long standing enmity between the family of accused-petitioner and deceased Minister for political reasons. 

 iii.	In Criminal Revision No. 123 of 2000 the proceeding of case remained stayed so far it related to co-accused Taheruddin Thakur and Criminal Revision is posted for hearing before a Division Bench presided over by Hasan Ameen, J. and case has been fixed for trial on 10.11.2001. 

 13. The law applicable to bail in non bailable offence is provided in Section 497 of The Code. Sub-section (1) of Section 497 postulates that an accused may not be released on bail if there appears reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The proviso to subsection contains exception to cases of a person being under the age of 16 years a woman or any sick or infirm. Under Section 498 of The Code both High Court Division and Court of Session can exercise discretionary power in extending concession of bail to an accused person. The power to grant bail under Section 498 of The Code is not additional to or independent of Section 497 and provisions contained in Section 497 have to be kept in view while granting bail under Section 498 of The Code. The discretionary power of High Court Division to grant freedom of bail under Section 498 of the Code is thus subservient and ancillary to Section 497 of The Code which limits the power to grant bail in a case punishable with death or imprisonment for life. 

 14. The court while considering a bail application tinder Section 498 of The Code is to take into account the nature and gravity of the offence and if the offence is of a kind in which bail should not be granted considering the gravity of offence, High Court Division should refuse to grant bail. The nature of charge is also a vital factor. The punishment to which the party may be liable, if convicted also bears upon the issue. In a charge of macabre murder where specific part is attributed to an accused, High Court Division will sparingly exercise its discretion in granting bail. It is only in very exceptional cases where life of an accused is in imminent danger established by Medical evidence that the discretion may be exercised in granting bail. 

 15. The soundness of the First Branch of contention is addressed now. In First Information Report it is positively stated that the accused petitioner along with other accused persons being armed with fire weapons indiscriminately fired upon former Minister Abdur Rab Serniabat, other members of the family and inmates of the house who died instantly sustaining bullet injuries and other members and inmates also sustained bullet injuries. Informant recognised the accused petitioner and other accused persons to be killers. Specific part has been attributed to the accused petitioner in the killing of former Minister Abdur Rab Serniabat, his grandson, a minor boy of 4 years, his daughter and other members of his family. The contention raised from the side of accused petitioner that he has been falsely implicated in the case out of political enmity cannot be gone into in disposing of an application for bail. Elaborate documentation of merit of the case is to be avoided while passing any order on bail application. It is stated here that on the order of a Division Bench of High Court Division to submit Police Report within 3.8.1997, Police submitted charge sheet on 30.7.1997 against accused petitioner and other accused persons. In investigation Police found complicity of the accused petitioner in commission of crime and laid charge sheet under Sections 120-B/149/448/326/307/302/201/297/34 of Penal Code. Learned Deputy Attorney General placed papers before us showing that charge had been framed against accused petitioner and other accused persons on 4.10.1999. It is stated here that charge sheet and charge had been framed during the pendency of this Criminal Miscellaneous Case. 

 17. This takes us to the Second branch of contention which is granting of bail on medical ground. A Division Bench of High Court Division at the time of issuance of Rule on 19.5.1997 did not grant ad-interim bail though medical ground was pressed for ad-interim bail. The Division Bench by order dated 2.7.1997 directed State opposite party to send accused petitioner for medical examination and treatment to P.G. Hospital. The accused petitioner was hospitalised in P.G. Hospital now Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital in compliance with order dated 2.7.1997. The Division Bench of High Court Division examined accused petitioner on 14.8.1997 in open court and found that the accused petitioner was ill and unable to move without any attendant. Still then the concession of ad-interim bail was not extended to accused petitioner. The Division Bench of High tester Division On 2..1.8.1997 recorded order that the accused petitioner be kept in P.G. Hospital till his recovery and before sending him back to Jail Hospital from P.P. Hospital, Director of Hospital would send a Report to Court for satisfaction so that it could direct for sending him back to custody. The Division Bench by order dated 28.8.1997 directed Jail Authority and P.G. Hospital Authority to treat accused petitioner as Divisional Prisoner. The Division Bench again by order dated 22.6.1998 directed the Director, P.O. Hospital to examine the health condition of accused petitioner and submit a Report about his health condition. On 19.8.1998 Criminal Miscellaneous Case was fixed for hearing on 24.8.1998. On 8.6.1999 again the Division Bench of High Court Division called for Report from Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital about the latest condition of health of the accused petitioner and also whether he needed further stay in the Hospital for receiving medical treatment and the Report was to come from a Medical Board constituted by Authorities of said Hospital. From record it appears that in compliance of the order of Court dated 21.8.1997 Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital Authority through Superintendent addressed to Assistant Registrar of the High Court Division of Supreme Court in Memo No. 13 SM MU/98/3080 dated 16.6.1998 sent Medical Report prepared by Medical Board consisting of Three (3) members and headed by Prof. Rashid-uddin Ahmad. The Report is dated 17.5.1998. Relevant portion of Medical Report is stated hereunder: 

 20. On examination of Reports of Medical Board consisting of Professors and Specialists of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital (former P.G. Hospital) it becomes manifestly clear that the case projected by accused-petitioner that he has been suffering from serious illness and he requires surgery stands negative and his stay in Hospital for treatment was not at all necessary. From the Medical Report it is not manifested that the life of the accused petitioner is in imminent danger and he is required to be freed by way of a bail. 

 22. Public Interest demands that Criminal Justice should be swift ensuring that the guilty persons are punished and innocent are absolved of charges. Article 35(3) of Bangladesh Constitution also, confers a right upon person accused of a Criminal offence to have a speedy trial Speedy trial in all circumstances; however, is not a hard and fast Rule. Nowadays trial cannot be expedited due to varieties of reasons such as, increasing number of eases seeking of adjournments both by Prosecution or the Defence, absconsion of accused persons collection of witnesses for production before court and other procedural hurdles. Delay in holding trials in all cases and circumstances is no good ground for granting bail to an accused person specially when he stands arraigned of a crime punishable with death or imprisonment for life. 

 23. In the case in hand eleven (11) accused persons are absconding and Criminal Revision No. 12:3 of 2000 filed by co-accused Taheruddin Thakore is pending before another Division Bench of High Court Division and proceedings of case remains stayed so far it related to that co-accused and said Criminal Revision is in list for hearing. From materials placed before us it appears that trial date is fixed on 10.11.200 1. Concession of bail to accused petitioner cannot be extended on the ground of delay in trial when the offence is grave in nature and there existed reasons for delay in commencement of trial and the trial is very much in sight and 10.11.2001 is set down for trial. 

 24. Let us now advert to the authorities placed from the side of accused-petitioner in support of contentions. Before adverting it is to be kept in view that a decision is only an authority for what it actually decides. It cannot be quoted for the proposition that may seem to follow from it. Every judgment must be read applicable to the particular facts proved or assumed to be proved. The generality of expression that may be found cannot be intended to be the exposition of whole law but must be regarded as governed or qualified by the particular facts of the case in which such expression occurs. It is neither desirable nor permissible to pick out a word or sentence from a judgment divorced from the context of the question under consideration and treat it to be complete law. 

 25. In Riasat Ali Vs Ghulam Muhammad and another 20 DLR SC 339, Leisurely steps taken in filing the challan, landy and halting production of evidence or seeking of unnecessary adjournments except those necessited by force of circumstances was strongly deprecated. It has been hold in that case that the delay in the prosecution of a case or the procrastination of the proceeding, in a trial furnishing as a ground for bail have to be weighed and judged in each case on its own merits. In that case there had been series of adjournments taken from the side of prosecution but in the case in hand trial did not commence. So cited case is quite distinguishable and got no bearing in the facts and circumstances of the present case. In Muslimuddin and others vs. The State, 1987 BLD AD 1 is not a case of bail and fundamental principle of criminal trial has been stated therein. The accused petitioner cannot have any assistance from the said authority. In A.K.M. Mosharaf Hossain vs. The State, 44 DLR AD 246 there was no incriminating materials other than the First Information Report wherefrom it could be inferred that there were reasonable grounds for believing that appellant (accused) had committed an offence. In the case in hand there are reasonable grounds which can lead to inference of the guilt of accused petitioner. This authority is also of no help to accused petitioner Master Giasuddin and others Vs. Stale 2 BLC AD 87 got no manner of application in the fact and circumstances of the present ease and it is not under-stood for what purpose this authority has been referred to. In State Vs. Jobaida Rashid, 49 DLR AD 199 High Court Division granted bail taking the view that there were no reasonable grounds for believing that the respondent (accused Johaida Rashid) had been guilty of the offence alleged and bait was not granted on the ground that she was sick and woman. The Appellate Division maintained the decision recorded by High Court Division. This decision is also, of no assistance to accused-petitioner. 

 26. We now propose to address ourselves to the authorities referred to from the side of State. In Major (Rtd) Mr. Khairuzzaman vs. The State, 18 BLD HCD 357 petition for bail of the accused petitioner Major (Rtd) M. Khairuzzaman who stands charged along with other accused persons for killing, of four National Leaders in Dhaka Central Jail on 3.11.1975 stood rejected taking into account the seriousness of the offence. Principles regulating grant or refusal of bail had been formulated in the said authority. The proposition of law enunciated in the said case is well recognised and well settled and no exception can be taken. In K.M. Obaidur Rahman and others vs. The State 51 DLR, HCD 51 bail petitions of accused petitioner K.M. Obaidur Rahman and others were rejected on the ground that there appeared reasonable grounds that the petitioners might be parties to a criminal conspiracy for killing four leaders in jail. Provision of Section 497(1) of The Code of Criminal Procedure in granting bail to accused persons guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life had been discussed. 

 Principles enunciated in the above cases are fully applicable in refusing bail to the accused petitioner. 

 27. Judging in the touchstone of the principles regulating grant or refusal of bail and taking into account the entire picture presented gravity of the offence and fact and circumstances of the case we are of this considered view that the accused petitioner cannot be at all favoured with concession of bail. 

 Charge had been framed against accused petitioner and other accused persons and the case is fixed for trial on 10.11.2001. In Criminal Revision No. 123 of 2000 proceeding of the case remains stayed with respect to co-accused Taheruddin Thakur and not with respect to other accused persons including accused petitioner and there cannot be any predicament in speedy trial with respect to accused petitioner and other accused-persons. The Trial Judge is directed to conclude trial as immediate as possible and for that purpose learned Trial Judge will exhaust all measures available under law and procedure and remove all procedural hurdles. 

 During pendency of this Criminal Miscellaneous Case a Division Bench of the High Court Division by Order dated 28.8.1997 directed the Jail Authorities of Dhaka Central Jail to treat the accused petitioner as a Division-I prisoner in the prison cell of P.G. Hospital during his stay there as patient. Taking into consideration the status of the accused petitioner we record direction upon Deputy Inspector General of Prison. Dhaka Central Jail Dhaka to give the accused petitioner the status of Division-1 prisoner in the jail. 

 31. On the premises of discussion made above and reasons stated, the inevitable corollary which flows is that Criminal Miscellaneous Case stands dismissed. Rule is, accordingly discharged. The accused petitioner is in Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital (former P.G. Hospital) since 27.8.1997. Medical Board recorded opinion that his stay in Hospital was not necessary. The Director of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Hospital (former P.G. Hospital) is directed to discharge the at petitioner from hospital and make arrangement to send him to Dhaka Central Jail. The State is, also, directed to make arrangement to send the accused petitioner to Dhaka Central Jail.
